keyframe_review.note: 858 km2; same cells as 1814 on the grid (the polygon is 107 km2 larger). The Congress of Vienna 'confirmed Hamburg's independence' and Hamburg became 'one of 39 sovereign states of the German Confederation (1815-1866)' (Hamburg page). Ritzebüttel is added as for 1814. Area check (repair pass): the States of the German Empire page, table row 'Hamburg | Free City | 414' (km2; the table gives no year for the area column, only 1871 and 1910 populations), against this shape's 858 km2: ratio 2.07 (the grid has the same three cells as 1814, 759 km2, ratio 1.83).

1,479 km2: the shape covers Ritzebüttel/Cuxhaven (one extra cell at 8.64E 53.83N, verified: the 1820 cells minus the 1814 cells is that single cell), matching the Cuxhaven page. AREA DECISION (repair pass): the States of the German Empire page gives Hamburg 414 km2 ('Free City', Empire period, no year for the area column; Bremen 256, Lübeck 298), so the polygons of 1820-1870 (1,436-1,479 km2) are 3.47 to 3.57 times the state. The table is right and the polygon's area is wrong, but its land cells are not: the resolved shape is four 253 km2 cells (1,012 km2) = the 1814 shape's three cells (city and Bergedorf, 759 km2) plus the Ritzebüttel cell. One cell is 61% of the whole state, so on this grid a city-state of 414 km2 that stretches from the city to the Elbe mouth cannot be drawn with fewer than three to four cells; the polygon's own bbox (8.37-10.36E, 53.39-53.94N) reaches west of Neuwerk (8.50E), so its extra area is Elbe estuary and tidal flats that carry no land cell. The outline is therefore kept (verdict ok) and the excess is grid granularity plus estuary water. The Geesthacht exclave (Landherrenschaft Bergedorf, Bergedorf page) lies at 10.37E, outside these cells and is not drawn. Against the 2016 infobox 755 km2 no like-for-like check exists (the modern city-state includes Altona, Harburg and Wandsbek, from 1937). Held to 1847 with no territorial change on any page opened.

region.text: 'Upon the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire in 1806' Hamburg 'became a sovereign state with the official title of the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg'

ledger.note: 1806: Hamburg becomes a sovereign state at the end of the Holy Roman Empire (Hamburg page: 'Upon the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire in 1806 ... became a sovereign state with the official title of the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg'). The page gives the year only (the HRE dossier dates the dissolution 6 August 1806) and names no territory; the land is the 1814 shape plus Ritzebüttel (Cuxhaven page: Hamburg's 'from the 13th century until 1937'), both the researcher's reading, hence confidence 2. Repair pass: the start moves from 1814 to 1806 because the same state 're-assumed its pre-1811 status' in 1814.

region.text: the city of Hamburg, 'occupied by the French army from 1806'

ledger.note: 1806: 'The cities of Hamburg and Bremen were occupied by the French army from 1806, following the end of the Prussian campaign' (Siege of Hamburg page). The page gives the year only; neither the Hamburg nor the History of Hamburg page mentions the occupation.

13 December 1810: the occupation turns into annexation. Whether French troops stayed in the city from 1806 to 1810 is on no page opened, so the end of the occupation is bridged at the annexation (as in free-city-of-lubeck).

region.text: the city of Hamburg, 'annexed to the French Empire on 13 December 1810'

ledger.note: 13 December 1810: France annexes Hamburg. Siege of Hamburg page: Hamburg and Bremen 'were annexed to the French Empire on 13 December 1810'; History of Hamburg page: 'Briefly annexed by Napoleon I (1810-14)'. Other pages differ by a year: Hamburg page '1804-1814/1815'; Bergedorf page 'formally annexed to the First French Empire as part of Bouches de l'Elbe département between 1811 and 1813'; Bouches-de-l'Elbe page: the department 'was formed in 1811'. first-french-empire /ledger/13 dates its gain 1811 (Territorial evolution of France page); this event takes the page's day, 13 December 1810, and the map changes in 1811.

region.text: Ritzebüttel (Cuxhaven), 'belonged to Hamburg from the 13th century until 1937' (53.861N 8.694E on the Cuxhaven page); a 10 km circle is a placement

ledger.note: 13 December 1810: Ritzebüttel goes with the city. The Cuxhaven page has Ritzebüttel in Hamburg's hands 'from the 13th century until 1937' and is silent on the French years; including it in the annexation is the researcher's reading, hence confidence 2.

region.text: the city of Hamburg, freed by Russian forces in 1814, which 're-assumed its pre-1811 status as a city-state'

ledger.note: May 1814: Hamburg is free again. Siege of Hamburg page: the siege ran '24 December 1813 to 12 May 1814' and the French garrison left 'on 27, 29, and 31 May 1814'; Hamburg page: 'Russian forces under General Bennigsen finally freed the city in 1814' and Hamburg 're-assumed its pre-1811 status as a city-state in 1814'. The Bouches-de-l'Elbe page: 'After Napoleon was defeated in 1814, the department were dissolved' and the area went to Hanover, Saxe-Lauenburg and the free cities of Hamburg and Lübeck. This replaces the earlier 'found' event, which gave the year only. The month 5 is the date of the garrison's departure.

region.text: Ritzebüttel (Cuxhaven), 'belonged to Hamburg from the 13th century until 1937' (53.861N 8.694E on the Cuxhaven page); a 10 km circle is a placement

ledger.note: 1814: Ritzebüttel at the Elbe mouth is again Hamburg's with the free city's restoration in May 1814. 'The city and its precursor Ritzebüttel belonged to Hamburg from the 13th century until 1937' (Cuxhaven page, which does not mention the French years); the 1814 date and the month are the researcher's reading from the restoration of the city, and Cliopatria adds the cell only in 1820. The 1810 loss above takes it away with the city.

region.text: Bergedorf, the condominium of Hamburg and Lübeck 1420-1867 (circle placed as in the Lübeck dossier; the page gives no area)

ledger.note: 1 January 1868: Hamburg takes over Lübeck's half of Bergedorf. 'Lübeck's sale of its share in the condominium to Hamburg in 1867', effective 1 January 1868 for 200,000 Prussian thaler; the cities had ruled the area jointly since the Peace of Perleberg of 1420 (formally annexed to France 1811-1813). Hamburg then formed the Landherrenschaft Bergedorf with Bergedorf and Geesthacht.

region.text: the state's outline as it stood in 1870, unchanged to November 1918

ledger.note: November 1918: Hamburg, a free city with no monarch, passes from the Empire's member states to a state of the Weimar Republic. 'In early November 1918, during the first days of the German revolution of 1918-1919' 'revolutionary workers and soldiers took over Hamburg's government with minimal violence or loss of life'; the city 'was to maintain its self-ruling status during the Weimar Republic (1919-33)' and a March 1919 Bürgerschaft election was to 'write a republican constitution for the city-state'. The German Empire page counts 'three free Hanseatic cities' among the 25 states. Federal state of the German Empire from 1871 ('The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty', German Empire page). Was a dissolve in 1871 into german-empire; moved to November 1918 and the counterpart changed to weimar-republic on the 3 Nov 2026 fix (fx-53 D01, as fx-46 R122 did for Bavaria): the Empire was this state's overlord, not its successor.

wars.name: Siege of Hamburg
wars.outcome: The siege ran from 24 December 1813 to 12 May 1814: the French garrison under Marshal Davout was besieged for over a year by Allied forces (mostly Russian, Swedish and German); it left Hamburg on 27, 29 and 31 May 1814 and Russian forces under General Bennigsen 'finally freed the city in 1814'.
wars.note: Dates from the Siege of Hamburg page (repair pass); the History of Hamburg page gives the year only. No contest events are recorded in this dossier because Hamburg was annexed (13 December 1810) and held by the First French Empire during the siege: the fighting is a contest between the Empire and the Allies, to be recorded in first-french-empire's ledger (it has none for Hamburg). The state is back in the ledger at the garrison's departure, 1814-5.

certainty.note: Cliopatria has no Hamburg shape before 1814 and no page gives a boundary; 1806-1810 uses the 1814 outline plus Ritzebüttel, 1811-1813 is French territory, 1814 is the restoration year.

A sovereign state of the German Confederation with defined territory, but the pages give no surveyed line; Bergedorf was a condominium with Lübeck to 1867, and Ritzebüttel and Neuwerk lay detached at the Elbe mouth. 1872-1918 (fx-53): the dossier records no frontier change after 1871; the state keeps its 1870 outline as a federal state of the German Empire.

notes: START (repair pass 2026-11-01, reviewer blocking fix): the dossier now starts in 1806. The Hamburg page makes Hamburg 'a sovereign state' upon the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire in 1806 and says it 're-assumed its pre-1811 status as a city-state in 1814', so it is one state; the earlier start in 1814 left 1806-1810 drawn by no dossier. The French years: occupied from 1806 (Siege of Hamburg page, year only; the Hamburg and History pages are silent, so no month is given and the November 1806 date of the Lübeck dossier is not applied), annexed on 13 December 1810 (Siege page), the department Bouches-de-l'Elbe 1811-1813/14 (Bergedorf and Bouches-de-l'Elbe pages), the siege 24 December 1813 to 12 May 1814, the garrison out 27-31 May 1814. The pages disagree on the annexation: 1804-1814/1815 (Hamburg), 1810-1814 (History), 13 December 1810 (Siege), 1811-1813 (Bergedorf, Bouches-de-l'Elbe); first-french-empire /ledger/13 dates its gain 1811 against this dossier's 1810-12 loss, and first-french-empire has no occupation of Hamburg from 1806 nor a contest event for the siege (to eu-20). The founding counterpart is holy-roman-empire-minor-states (the HRE 1260-1806 dossier, which has no Hamburg event). AREA (repair pass): the 1820-1870 polygons (1,436-1,479 km2) are 3.5 times (3.47 to 3.57) the 414 km2 of the States of the German Empire table (no year; Empire period); the table is right, the outline is kept because the resolved grid is four 253 km2 cells (the 1814 city and Bergedorf cells plus Ritzebüttel) and nothing smaller is possible; see the 1820 keyframe. RITZEBÜTTEL: Cliopatria adds the Cuxhaven cell only in 1820; the Cuxhaven page has it Hamburg's to 1937 without a gap, so it is added from the start (1806) in the founding region, lost with the city in 1810-12 and regained in 1814-5 (confidence 2). Neuwerk is called a Hamburg dependency without dates and is not drawn (no land cell within 12 km of 8.50E 53.92N). BERGEDORF: held jointly with Lübeck until 31 December 1867; Cliopatria draws it as Hamburg's from 1814, the Lübeck dossier counts it as Lübeck's, so it is drawn twice until 1868. Geesthacht (Bergedorf's exclave) is not drawn. END: like the other German states of the group, the dossier ends in 1871 with the German Empire as successor; Hamburg remained a state to 1937 and beyond. The page budget (5) was spent in the first pass; the repair pass opened the Siege of Hamburg and States of the German Empire pages and reopened Hamburg, History of Hamburg and Bergedorf at the reviewer's request. Gazetteer: Cuxhaven/Ritzebüttel, Bergedorf and Neuwerk are not place names in the gazetteer (circles used); the Hamburg dossier needs no new region names. Counterparts: first-french-empire, holy-roman-empire-minor-states, free-city-of-lubeck, german-empire, swedish-empire and russian-empire are dossiers of other groups. REALM OF MEMBER STATES (fx-53 D01, 3 Nov 2026): this state now lives to November 1918 as a federal state of the German Empire, which 'retained their own governments' (German Empire page: 'The other states retained their own governments but had only limited aspects of sovereignty'; 'the Kaiser and all German ruling kings, dukes, and princes abdicated' in November 1918) and the German revolution of 1918-1919 page: 'By the end of the month, the dynastic rulers of all the other German states had abdicated without bloodshed'. Changed: identity.end 1871 -> 1918/11; the 1871 dissolve into german-empire became a 1918/11 dissolve into weimar-republic; successors german-empire -> weimar-republic; last keyframe (free-city-of-hamburg_1870) carried to 1918 ('to'); capital and certainty to 1918. The german-empire dossier no longer gains this land in 1871 nor lists the state as a predecessor, and weimar-republic lists it as a predecessor (fx-53 D02, D04). The hierarchy.csv row free-city-of-hamburg -> german-empire (constituent, 1871-1918) is for the orchestrator. A free city: no abdication; the page gives 'early November 1918' for the revolution and the dissolve is dated November 1918.
